Alright, let me think about this year...

I've been doing this for thirty years, same land, same wheat-maize. My father did it before me. Six and a half mu isn't much — my son works in town now, so it's mostly me and my wife in the field. We manage.

**Wheat first.** I'll plant around October 10th, maybe a few days later if it stays warm. I use the seed I bought from the shop — same variety the village has been planting, I don't remember the name but the shop owner knows what I want. About 30 jin per mu (15 kg). Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the one with three 15s on the bag — that's always worked. Plow it in with the neighbor's tractor, he does my field for a small fee.

Come spring, when the wheat starts standing up tall at jointing, I put down half a bag of urea per mu. If it looks yellow I put a bit more. Irrigate once before winter, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling — three times usually, unless the rain helps. The well costs money to run, so I don't waste water. Spray once for weeds when I see them coming up in spring.

Last year I got about 450 kg/mu. Year before was worse, maybe 400, dry spring. If the weather is normal I expect around 450 again.

**Then maize right after wheat harvest in June.** No time to plow — I have the neighbor drill the maize seed right into the stubble, same day or next day after I finish threshing. Hybrid seed, the red bag kind, that's what everyone plants. One bag compound per mu at planting. When the maize is about knee-high I side-dress half a bag of urea. If July and August rain normally, I don't irrigate. If it's dry at tasseling I'll pump once. Spray herbicide when the weeds come.

Maize usually gives me about 500 kg/mu. Harvest end of September, dry it on the road or the roof, then turn around and plant wheat again.

Money is tight so I can't put down more fertilizer than this. My neighbor Old Wang tried putting on less one year to save money and his wheat was thin — I won't risk that. Better to spend the fertilizer money and have grain in the bin.
